第 65 章 People Leave Bad Managers, Not Bad Jobs—Right?人们离开坏经理，不是坏工作——对吧？

Nik Knight / 尼克·奈特

— 第 185 页 —

You will often hear that people don't leave bad jobs, they leave bad managers. As with many meme-friendly pearls of wisdom, there is far more to it than that; sometimes people do leave because of problems with their boss, but there are a whole host of other factors that push or pull people to a new opportunity. Before I go further, full disclosure: I've been a manager for around 10 years now, and in that time, a number of direct and indirect reports have left my team. Each one had their reasons for leaving, and I freely admit that for some, I was at least part of that reason. So, this is not a defensive reaction on my part—I haven't always been the manager people have needed or deserved, and I'm not too proud to admit that. It was all part of my development as a leader, and I only hope that I didn't do too much damage to others in the process.

你会经常听到人们不是离开坏工作，而是离开坏经理。和很多适合做表情包的智慧 pearls 一样，远不止如此；有时候人们确实因为老板的问题离开，但还有一大堆其他因素推或拉人们到新机会。在我继续之前，完全坦白：我做经理大约 10 年了，在这段时间里，一些直接和间接下属离开了我的团队。每个人都有他们离开的理由，我坦然承认对其中一些人，我至少是那个原因的一部分。所以这不是我这边的防御反应——我并不总是人们需要或应得的经理，我不会太骄傲而不承认。这都是我作为领导发展的一部分，我只希望我在这个过程中没有对别人造成太多伤害。

Having said that, there were a good many reasons for people deciding to move on that were beyond my ability to influence. Partners got job offers in other parts of the world. Some people—especially those in the early stages of their careers—worked out that actually, they weren't on the right path for them. Or in the right city. Or earning the right salary. For some, opportunities arose that were just too good to turn down. The greatest line manager in the world would struggle to compete in these scenarios.

话虽如此，人们决定离开有很多超出我影响能力的原因。伴侣在世界其他地方拿到工作机会。有些人——尤其是职业生涯早期的人——想通了其实他们不在适合自己的道路上。或者不在对的城市。或者没拿到对的薪水。对一些人来说，出现了太好了无法拒绝的机会。世界上最好的直线经理在这些场景下也难以竞争。

Deciding to change jobs is rarely due to a single root cause—what decision ever is, really?—it's often a multidimensional thing, even though there might be a catalyst that finally tips people over from "meh" to "I'm outta here!" This is the space where a good manager can make a difference and pull someone who is wavering back from the edge.

决定换工作很少因为单一根本原因——哪个决定真的是呢？——它通常是多维的事情，即使可能有一个催化剂最终把人们从「 meh 」推到「我走人！」这是好经理可以产生影响、把摇摆的人从边缘拉回来的空间。

— 第 186 页 —

A line manager who is interested in their team members' well-being, checks in frequently, monitors morale, and so on, stands a far better chance of spotting the warning signs of a flight risk, and can therefore choose to address problems early. An opportunity to learn a new skill, a change of project, a tweak to working hours—there's a million things that could make a world of difference to someone struggling to find the joy in their day-to-day routine. Of course, there's nothing to stop any manager from doing this—those who don't aren't necessarily bad managers though, they are just not yet proficient at this skill.

一个关心团队成员福祉、经常检查、监控士气的直线经理，更有可能发现离职风险的警告信号，从而选择尽早解决问题。一个学新技能的机会、换项目、微调工作时间——有一百万件事可以给一个在日常中挣扎找快乐的人带来天壤之别。当然，没有什么阻止任何经理这么做——那些不做的人不一定是坏经理，他们只是还不精通这个技能。

Sometimes, though, even when they have a diligent, caring manager who's totally on top of what their team needs and how to keep them engaged, people still opt to take the path out. This generally points to a bigger problem—the team culture might be healthy, but perhaps the organizational culture is not. I saw a beautifully succinct description of this in a tweet not long ago; "good managers know when to amplify or dampen corporate leadership." I have seen the more talented managers I've encountered do exactly this—but there are limits to how much one person can dampen the effects of a toxic environment. Does this make them a bad manager? Not so much.

然而有时候，即使有一个勤勉、关心人的经理，完全掌握团队需要什么和怎么保持他们投入，人们仍然选择离开。这通常指向更大的问题——团队文化可能健康，但组织文化可能不健康。不久前我在一条推文中看到一个优美简洁的描述；「好经理知道什么时候放大或抑制公司领导层的影响。」我见过我遇到的更有才华的经理正是这么做的——但一个人能抑制有毒环境影响的程度是有限的。这让他们成为坏经理吗？倒也不是。

So, is there such a thing as a "bad manager" at all? Well, there are certainly people for whom management does not come naturally. For some of these folks, it is a skill they will never quite master, and unfortunately, there are others who don't even see the need to try. There are teams and organizations where developing management and leadership skills just isn't a priority, or where command-and-control is still seen as the standard way to manage. It's not impossible to improve these situations, but it can be exhausting swimming against that tide—there must be the will to change in the mix somewhere.

那到底有没有「坏经理」这种东西？当然，有些人天生不擅长管理。对这些人中的一些，这是他们永远不会完全掌握的技能，不幸的是，还有另一些人甚至不觉得需要尝试。有些团队和组织，发展管理和领导技能根本不是优先事项，或者命令控制仍然被视为标准管理方式。改善这些情况不是不可能，但逆着潮水游泳可能令人精疲力竭——必须在某个地方有改变的意愿。

Do people leave people who are (currently) doing a not-so-great job of management? Hell, yes! Is that the only reason they leave? No. Not by a long shot. The best thing we can do as managers is to regularly take a long, hard, clear-eyed look at ourselves and ask, "Am I being the manager this person, this team needs me to be?" If the answer is yes, great—good for you, keep going. If not, maybe it's time to think about what you could change that would make a real difference to the team you serve.

人们会离开那些（目前）管理工作做得不那么好的人吗？当然会！那是他们离开的唯一原因吗？不是。远远不是。作为经理我们能做的最好的事情是定期长期、认真、清醒地审视自己，问：「我在做这个人、这个团队需要我做的经理吗？」如果答案是是，太好了——不错，继续。如果不是，也许是时候想想你可以改变什么，会对你服务的团队产生真正影响。
